Veeam.title: Autonomy Is Only Safe When It Is Reversible
Veeam.summary: Somewhere in your organization, an AI agent has permission to do real work. It reads records, updates systems, moves data, and finishes tasks without asking anyone, which is exactly what you hired it for. The same permission that lets it work also lets it do damage. And there’s no version of the agent that gets one without the other. The post Autonomy Is Only Safe When It Is Reversible appeared first on Veeam Software Official Blog .

This review resulted in software hardening releases that address multiple internally discovered vulnerabilities. These vulnerabilities were found during internal testing and are not known to be actively exploited. VMware.summary: (Day 12 of 22 in our Cybersecurity Awareness Month series. Today: VM snapshots) Snapshots might be the most underrated security tool in VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF). They are why you can patch a guest operating system on a weekday afternoon without holding your breath, how you can preserve evidence from a compromised system before anyone … Continued The post Snapshots Are Your Best Friend appeared first on VMware Blogs .

AWS.title: [Preview Announcement] Re-introducing Forward Proxy as AWS Network Firewall Functionality
AWS.summary: You can now use your Network Firewall with all its existing filtering capabilities and features as an explicit forward proxy. On Nov 25, 2025, AWS introduced Network Firewall proxy in public preview to help customers exert centralized security controls against data exfiltration and malware injection. At the time, the Network Firewall proxy was introduced as a standalone product, separate from Network Firewall transparent firewall and used its own separate proxy security policy.
